title: QBR — Uptime & FinOps playbook + model rollout sync
summary: Quarterly health check focused on uptime SLAs, cost variances from last quarter, and upcoming model rollout. Redwood reviewed FinOps suggestions (batching & quantization) and reliability mitigations (regional fallback + canary rollouts). Customer raised concerns about spikes during Black Friday trial and SSO/audit log needs for finance and security teams. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run a short-headroom stress test, provide updated pricing scenarios, and share SOC2 evidence and KMS integration notes.
topics: Pilot roadmap: model v2 rollout (canary & fallback)
Security/compliance checklist: SSO, audit logs, KMS
action_items: Jordan: Send three pricing scenarios (hosted, dedicated baseline, dedicated + burst) by 2025-07-18
Maya: Share a short runbook for canary + automatic fallback and a sample canary config by 2025-07-20
Liam: Schedule 90-min stress run with BlueMarina SREs to validate headroom (proposed window 2025-07-22)
Sofia: Provide target success metrics for v2 rollout (latency p50/p95, error budget) by 2025-07-17
next_steps: Redwood to run 1-hour headroom test and share results
Customer to confirm procurement timeline for Dedicated capacity if stress test shows need
Redwood to attach SOC2 summary + KMS integration doc to the shared folder
Follow-up meeting: 2025-07-23 15:00 UTC for test results and pilot decision
transcript: Meeting header: 2025-07-15 15:00 UTC — duration ~48m; Recording started
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neil (Redwood CSM) — Sofia Ramirez (BlueMarina, Head of ML), Ethan Cole (VP Eng), Priya Singh (FinOps), Daniel Park (SRE)
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time — quick roll call?
[00:10] Sofia: Yep Sofia here, hi all
[00:12] Ethan: Ethan — running a bit off today but here
[00:15] Priya: Priya — FinOps, good to be here
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: usage & cost delta, uptime trends, v2 model rollout plan, security asks. We'll keep to 45-ish minutes and then capture next steps
[02:01] Maya: I'll jump into the metrics; pulling up a screen share (noise) — okay traffic last quarter saw a 42% spike in token volume around the new recommendation feature launch
[02:30] Maya: p50 latency is stable at 120ms for hosted, p95 creeped to 780ms during peak rolling window — that's where the user impact was reported
[03:05] Daniel: To be clear the 780 was during a cascading retry loop — our infra traced it to a cold KV cache on the edge nodes
[03:22] Jordan: Right — that matches Redwood traces, we saw a drop in cache hit-rate when the prefix patterns changed after the new prompt library deploy
[04:10] Sofia: We're most worried about a similar pattern happening during holiday peak (Black Friday test). If that occurs we need failover behavior — do you support regional fallback?

[04:30] Maya: Yes we do — there are two routing policies: latency-first and cost-first. For emergencies we can flip to a higher-tier region or a larger model variant with automatic fallback. There was a little glitch in the route-policy we diagnosed last month but patch is in place
[05:12] Ethan: What's the unit-cost delta if we go to dedicated vs hosted for sustained peak traffic? Priya is on the line
[05:25] Priya: yes cost sensitivity is high. Our CFO wants worst-case burn scenarios

[05:40] Jordan: We'll provide three scenarios — hosted (pay-as-you-go), dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) and dedicated with burst overlay. Each will show per-token and instance cost, plus amortized networking
[06:05] Jordan: Quick note — some of our batching and quantization suggestions could save 20-35% on token cost without measurably changing latency for your workloads
[06:30] Priya: How intrusive is quantization? We can't afford output regressions on product-critical prompts

[06:45] Maya: We recommend a small eval harness — Redwood Optimize can run automated prompt-level regressions and flag changes. For many retrieval-heavy prompts, 8-bit quantization hit was negligible in our benchmarks
[07:15] Sofia: Would you run that on our dev prompts? We can share a sanitized prompt set
[07:25] Maya: Absolutely — if you share a small representative subset we can run a quick regression prior to the pilot
[08:00] Daniel: On the reliability side we want to lock down alerting thresholds. What's the standard error budget SLA you expose in the console?

[08:20] Liam: The Console exposes token-level latency and error-rate thresholds per route and per model; we can hook in PagerDuty and ship a default SLO dashboard. We'll also provide an incident runbook template
[08:50] Daniel: Do you capture request-level audit logs? Security wants retention details

[09:05] Jordan: Yes — request and response metadata (note: full response bodies are redacted by default) — logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or stored in a customer-managed S3 with configurable retention. We also have KMS/HSM options for key management
[09:35] Priya: And SOC2? Our procurement wants that paperwork
[09:40] Jordan: We'll attach the SOC2 Type II summary and a short compliance pack after this meeting
[10:05] Ethan: Back to rollout: v2 model is larger — any recommendations to keep latency stable during canary?

[10:22] Maya: Canary should be traffic-weighted and ramped over 48–72 hours. Use prefix caching and shorter KV warms to avoid cold starts. Also enable continuous batching for canary routes — that smooths out p95 spikes
[11:00] Sofia: For evals our target is p50 < 150ms, p95 < 500ms and error rate < 0.1% during steady state. If those aren't hit during canary we halt rollout
[11:22] Maya: Noted — we'll codify that canary policy in the rollout config. We can also set automatic fallback to v1 if p95 breaches 600ms for 5 minutes
[12:14] Jordan: Financially, if dedicated is needed we recommend a baseline pool sized for 95th percentile disk and GPU utilization with autoscale headroom of 20%
[12:40] Priya: Curious, your Optimize tool flagged a potential 18% saving by changing batch windows — what are the tradeoffs?

[12:55] Maya: Increasing maximum batch latency tolerance can improve throughput but might add a few ms to p50. For low-latency endpoints you can apply adaptive batching only to non-real-time routes or use response streaming
[13:30] Ethan: Could you run a simulated Black Friday hour with our pattern? We want to see if the headroom holds
[13:45] Liam: We can — propose a 90-min stress test at low risk hours. We'll coordinate with Daniel's SREs for a traffic replay
[14:10] Daniel: Preferred window is 2025-07-22 02:00–03:30 UTC — off-peak for our customers
[14:25] Jordan: Perfect — we'll confirm via calendar invite and include the runbook
[15:00] Sofia: Small nit: we need audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance and SSO tied to Okta with role-based RBAC for dev/prod separation
[15:18] Maya: Okta SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning is supported. For RBAC we can map roles to Console permissions, and audit log forwarding to Splunk is in the integration guide
[16:05] Priya: Procurement/finance will also need pricing committed for the pilot period — what's the cadence?
[16:20] Jordan: We'll do a 30-day pilot pricing deck and a projected three-tier pricing for scaling scenarios. I'll circulate that by Friday 2025-07-18
[17:00] Ethan: On the technical side, any limitations with private deployments / VPC if we choose to go that route later?

[17:15] Maya: Private deployment supports customer-managed VPC, on-prem packaging, and can integrate with your HSM. There is some deployment lead time (~6–8 weeks) and we usually recommend Dedicated as an intermediate if speed matters
[18:02] Sofia: Also question from the product team: will there be any change in embedding semantics between v1 and v2? We use embeddings for rerank and similarity
[18:20] Maya: Embedding behavior can shift slightly; we'll include a similarity-preservation eval as part of the rollout. If drift is observed we can pin embedding model for rerank routes
[19:10] Daniel: Thoughts on cold KV cache mitigation — warmers? we've seen issues where the cache TTLs are too short
[19:25] Maya: We recommend proactive prefix warming and a tiered cache TTL policy; also use sticky sessions for a short warm-up window during canary
[20:05] Jordan: Quick recap before we run out: action items (pricing, runbook, stress test), security docs, and pilot decision timeline
[20:25] Sofia: Sounds good. One last ask — can Redwood provide an annotated playbook for outage scenarios we can integrate into our oncall runbooks?
[20:40] Liam: Yes — we'll deliver a 3-page outage playbook and a runbook template you can adopt
[21:00] Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with the invite for 2025-07-22 stress test and the pricing spreadsheet by 2025-07-18. Any other pressing items?
[21:20] Priya: Nothing further from FinOps, thanks
[21:25] Ethan: All good, thanks everyone
[21:30] Sofia: Thanks — appreciate the clear action plan
[21:45] Jordan: Thanks all — meeting adjourned, will share notes and files
Meeting end: 15:48 UTC — Recording stopped
